summary: Unexpected egress reroute in us-west-2 causing tail-latency spikes and streaming cancellations for Acme Health
description: Issue summary: Between ~2026-03-12 14:10 UTC and ongoing, Acme Health reported a sharp increase in p95/p99 inference latency and a rise in streaming request cancellations originating from their dedicated cluster in us-west-2. Impact: Customer-facing inference calls experienced timeouts and client-side stream disconnects; retries caused request duplication for a subset of traffic. Scope: Only Acme Health's dedicated pool in us-west-2 observed the behavior; other dedicated customers in the same region show intermittent, lower-severity spikes.
timeline: 2026-03-12 14:05 UTC - First alert from Acme (support@acmehealth.com). 14:12 UTC - Automated SLO alert (p99 > 3.5s) for Acme routing shard. 14:18 UTC - Support triage; assigned to on-call SRE. 14:25 UTC - Observed concurrent increase in egress path latency and TCP retransmits on the regional egress-proxy. 15:05 UTC - Temporary policy applied to bypass recently added egress-peering route; partial improvement. 16:00 UTC - Follow-up: spike recurred when load increased; investigation continues.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send streaming generate requests to customer's dedicated endpoint in us-west-2 with typical prompt size. 2) Observe initial token latency under normal conditions, then repeat under burst load (200 concurrent clients). 3) Note p95/p99 token latencies rising to >3s and stream connection resets consistent with client-side cancellations. Reproducible during the spike window.
observed_logs_and_metrics: - Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.internal/redwood/prod/egress/us-west-2 (p99 token time jumped from 850ms -> 3.9s). - nginx/egress-proxy logs: increased 502s and backend connection reset entries tied to backend IPs from peer BGP range. - tcpdump on egress-proxy: elevated retransmits and out-of-order segments. - Serving runtime traces show longer queue wait times due to upstream egress slowdowns.
initial_hypothesis: A recent egress peering advertisement or route preference change caused a subset of traffic to be forwarded over a higher-latency transit path (AS-path hop increase), increasing RTT and causing streaming timeouts. The egress-proxy did not fail over cleanly between routes under burst load, exposing tail latency.
investigation_notes: Checked recent network changes: Ops deployed egress peering change at 2026-03-12 13:58 UTC (see INT-4027).
BGP path analysis: several prefixes used by customer traffic now prefer a transit announced by partner X with 2 additional AS hops relative to previous path.
Correlation: p99 spikes aligned with periods of increased load and when the proxy chose the new path during connection establishment.
Reproduced locally by forcing route selection via traffic-engineering flags; confirmed higher latency and TCP retransmits on that path.

Workaround applied: pinned affected egress prefixes to original peer via emergency policy; immediate p95/p99 improvement observed (~40% reduction), but not fully stable under peak burst due to intermittent failover behavior.
Observability gap: egress-proxy health checks do not currently capture elevated RTTs before backend connection resets; adding latency probes to the runbook.
Related: linked to SUP-19911 where a similar pattern occurred in eu-west but with different root cause (transit saturation).
comments: Maya Chen (2026-03-12 14:20): Customer reports streaming sessions drop after ~6-12 tokens. Asked for request ids and example timestamps; customer provided sample ids: req_akj-3382, req_akj-3387.
Sanjay Rao (SRE) (2026-03-12 14:35): Started capturing tcpdumps on egress-proxy; initial signs point to path change. Eng paging alerted network team.
Lena Morales (Network Eng) (2026-03-12 15:00): Confirmed a change in route preference from partner peer B. Rolling back announcement should reestablish prior AS-path. Preparing rollback play.
Support (2026-03-12 15:12): Applied emergency egress pin for Acme prefixes; customer confirms perceptible improvement but intermittent failures persist at scale.
Customer (Acme Health) (2026-03-12 15:30): Noted fewer errors after policy but still seeing elevated tail latency during peak times. Requesting ETA and a durable fix.

Sanjay Rao (2026-03-12 16:05): Identified additional issue: egress-proxy's connection pool logic delays fallback to alternative healthy upstreams under burst conditions; filing INT-4123 to fix connection failover behavior.
Maya Chen (2026-03-12 16:20): Updating customer that we have a temporary mitigation and ETA for network rollback is 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC; will follow up with permanent remediation plan.
next_steps: 1) Network: rollback peering preference for affected prefixes to original peer (scheduled 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC). 2) Engineering: patch egress-proxy connection pool to fail fast to healthiest upstreams (INT-4123). 3) Add latency-health probes and SLO alerts for egress backends. 4) Post-incident: runbook update and blameless postmortem with engineering, network, and support.
workaround: Emergency egress pinning applied for Acme prefixes (immediate improvement).
Short-term: advise customer to stagger client reconnects and increase client-side stream keepalive to reduce amplification of retries.
notes: Priority elevated due to P0 customer impact on production inference. Keep updates concise and include concrete timestamps for correlation.
